submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3.5 cm thickness provides the best pion/kaon separation (3.8 sigma at 10 GeV/c) among radiators that can meet the humidity ageing requirement. While Radiator-R1 shows higher separation (4.66 sigma at 2.5 cm), it is a porous radiator without hydrophobic treatment and is therefore unlikely to meet the hard constraint of <10% transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing. Radiator-R3's hydrophobic treatment specifically addresses humidity resistance, making it suitable for long-term operation where the radiator cannot be replaced. Radiator-R2, while likely meeting the humidity requirement as a solid material, provides significantly lower separation (2.9 sigma). The 3.5 cm thickness was determined through systematic simulation to be optimal for R3, showing peak performance in the allowed 1-6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 at 3.5 cm provides 3.8 sigma separation, which is the best achievable performance among radiators that meet the humidity ageing constraint. While R1 could achieve 4.66 sigma, it likely fails the humidity requirement.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is one of the three candidates: R1 (high-index porous), R2 (solid, lower index), and R3 (porous with hydrophobic treatment).

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 has hydrophobic treatment specifically to address humidity concerns. As a porous radiator with this treatment, it is designed to resist moisture-induced transparency loss. This distinguishing feature mentioned in the specs implies R3 passes the humidity ageing test, unlike R1 which lacks such treatment.
The recommended thickness of 3.5 cm is within the allowed range of 1-6 cm.
